title: Augmented internal homogeneous bar resolution
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, and write $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$ for its condensed group. Work with internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and with $A$-linear actions of $\underline G$ and equivariant module morphisms. For a condensed set $X$, let $A[X]$ denote the free internal $A$-module, the left adjoint of the forgetful functor to condensed sets. Define $P_n=A[\underline G^{n+1}]$ for $n\geq0$, with diagonal left $G$-action, and let $A$ have trivial action. The augmentation $\epsilon:P_0\to A$ sends each generator $[g]$ to $1$. For $n\geq1$ set
$$\partial_n[g_0,\ldots,g_n]=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i[g_0,\ldots,\widehat{g_i},\ldots,g_n].$$
These are morphisms of internal equivariant modules, satisfy $\epsilon\partial_1=0$ and $\partial_n\partial_{n+1}=0$, and the augmented complex $\cdots\to P_1\to P_0\to A\to0$ is exact. More generally, for every internal $A$-module $T$, with trivial $G$-action, the augmented complex obtained by tensoring over $A$ with $T$ is exact. Here tensor is the internal module tensor product, and exactness means equality of the image and kernel subobjects, including surjectivity of the augmentation. Under the continuous change of coordinates
$$(g_0,\ldots,g_n)\longleftrightarrow(g_0,g_0^{-1}g_1,g_1^{-1}g_2,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n),$$
the object $P_n$ is the induced equivariant module $A[\underline G]\otimes_A A[\underline G^n]$, where $G$ acts by left translation on the first factor only. No categorical projectivity of $A[\underline G^n]$ is asserted.

WANTED: an ordinary condensed-module reference for this internal resolution; the ordinary abstract-group theorem is only an analogy.

proof.text: First transfer the statement to sheaves of modules. Since $A$ is a commutative condensed ring, its reconstructed section-ring sheaf is $A$ itself, and [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] gives an equivalence $E_A$ from internal $A$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] to $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, sheaves of $A$-modules, leaving underlying abelian sheaves, sections and morphisms unchanged; in particular it commutes with the forgetful functors to condensed sets, so it carries free internal modules to free objects of $\mathcal M$, and it carries kernel, image and cokernel subobjects to the same subsheaves. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E_A$ is exact and carries the internal relative tensor product to $\otimes_A$ of $\mathcal M$, with $E_A(A)=A$ and pure tensors $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$, compatibly with associators and unitors. Hence every assertion of the statement, including the tensored complexes, may be proved in $\mathcal M$, which all remaining steps do. For a condensed set $X$, form the presheaf $F_X(S)=A(S)[X(S)]$ of free $A(S)$-modules; restriction sends $a[x]$ to $a|_T[x|_T]$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], its module sheafification $F_X^\#$ exists and maps from it to an $A$-module sheaf $M$ are exactly presheaf-module maps $F_X\to M$. Such a map is uniquely specified by a natural assignment $x\mapsto m_x\in M(S)$, by the formula $\sum a_x[x]\mapsto\sum a_xm_x$. These assignments are exactly maps of condensed sets $X\to M$. Thus $F_X^\#$ realizes the free module $A[X]$ specified in the statement. For any map $u:X\to Y$, its linearization is $[x]\mapsto[u(x)]$; equalities between linearized maps can be checked on these generators before sheafification. For the terminal sheaf $1$, $F_1=A$, so $A[1]=A$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; free-module construction in proof of lemma-universal-module, applied to A[X].

proof.text:
For condensed sets $X,Y$, sectionwise bilinear extension gives inverse maps
$$A(S)[X(S)]\otimes_{A(S)}A(S)[Y(S)]\ \rightleftarrows\ A(S)[X(S)\times Y(S)],\qquad [x]\otimes[y]\longleftrightarrow[(x,y)].$$
The inverse respects the tensor relations because $(\sum a_x[x],\sum b_y[y])$ is sent to $\sum_{x,y}a_xb_y[(x,y)]$; both composites are the identity on generating tensors or generators. These maps commute with restriction. Sheafify and use [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] with ring presheaf $A=A^\#$ to obtain
$$A[X]\otimes_A A[Y]\cong A[X\times Y].$$
The displayed maps, their inverses and their compatibility with maps of $X,Y$ are retained. This is a calculation with free modules, not an assertion that their sections after sheafification are sectionwise free.

If a condensed group acts on $X$, linearize its action map $\underline G\times X\to X$ and use the isomorphism of step 2 to obtain $A[\underline G]\otimes_A A[X]\to A[X]$. On generators this is $[g]\otimes[x]\mapsto[gx]$; the group laws are verified on $[g]\otimes[h]\otimes[x]$. Consequently the diagonal actions on $P_n$ are internal $A$-linear actions. Deleting coordinate $i$ is a continuous equivariant map $G^{n+1}\to G^n$, since deletion of $(gg_0,\ldots,gg_n)$ is $g$ times the deleted tuple. Its linearization is therefore an equivariant module map. Their signed sum is $\partial_n$. The map to $A=A[1]$ induced by $\underline G\to1$ is the stated augmentation and is equivariant for the trivial action. For actions on an arbitrary module sheaf, sectionwise extension on $A(S)[G(S)]\times M(S)$ is bilinear and natural; [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] uniquely extends it after sheafifying the first factor, since the second factor and target are already sheaves. The tensor universal property then gives the corresponding action map. Its uniqueness justifies checking equivariance on group generators and arbitrary module sections.

proof.text: On a generator $[g_0,g_1]$, $\epsilon\partial_1=1-1=0$. In $\partial_n\partial_{n+1}$, fix two original indices $0\le i<j\le n+1$. Deleting $j$ and then $i$ contributes sign $(-1)^{j+i}$; deleting $i$ and then original $j$ (now at index $j-1$) contributes $(-1)^{i+j-1}$. The resulting tuple is identical and the coefficients sum to zero. Every ordered double deletion belongs to exactly one such pair. Thus the composite is zero on every generator and hence zero as an internal module map by step 1.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the internal homogeneous bar input.

proof.text:
Forget the $G$-action for the following maps. The continuous insertion $G^{n+1}\to G^{n+2}$, $(g_0,\ldots,g_n)\mapsto(1,g_0,\ldots,g_n)$, gives $h_n:P_n\to P_{n+1}$. Set $h_{-1}:A\to P_0$ to be $a\mapsto a[1]$. Then $\epsilon h_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_A$. Expanding the differential on an inserted tuple gives, for $n\ge1$,
$$\partial_{n+1}h_n[g_0,\ldots,g_n]=[g_0,\ldots,g_n]-h_{n-1}\partial_n[g_0,\ldots,g_n].$$
Indeed deleting the inserted $1$ is the first term, and deleting original coordinate $i$ has sign $(-1)^{i+1}$, the negative of its sign in $h_{n-1}\partial_n$. In degree zero the expansion is $\partial_1h_0[g]=[g]-[1]$, so $\partial_1h_0+h_{-1}\epsilon=\mathrm{id}_{P_0}$. These generator equalities give identities of sheaf-module morphisms. No equivariance of $h_n$ is required or claimed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the internal homogeneous bar input.

proof.text:
The underlying module category is abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian], applied to the small site in the statement and its commutative ring sheaf $A$. Put $d_0=\epsilon$ and $d_n=\partial_n$ for $n\ge1$. For the kernel inclusion $k_n:K_n\to P_n$, step 5 yields
$$k_n=d_{n+1}h_nk_n+h_{n-1}d_nk_n=d_{n+1}h_nk_n.$$
Thus $k_n$ factors through $d_{n+1}$, so $\ker d_n\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}$. The reverse inclusion follows from step 4. This proves exactness at every $P_n$ in underlying modules. The identity $\epsilon h_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_A$ proves that the augmentation is a split epimorphism there, giving exactness at $A$ as well.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the internal homogeneous bar input.

proof.text: To justify exactness in equivariant modules, set $B=A[\underline G]$ in $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(A)$. Step 2 linearizes group multiplication to $B\otimes_A B\to B$ with $[g]\otimes[h]\mapsto[gh]$, and gives unit $A\to B$, $1\mapsto[1]$. Associativity and unity are generator equalities. An internal linear $G$-action on $M$ gives the $B$-module action $[g]\otimes m\mapsto gm$ by linear extension; conversely restrict a $B$-module action to the generators $g\mapsto[g]$. These constructions are inverse because linear maps from a free module are determined on its generators; the module laws become the group-action laws, and $g^{-1}$ provides the inverse action. The morphism conditions also agree. Thus equivariant modules and their forgetful functor are the $B$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] in $\mathcal M$ and their forgetful functor. Here $B$ is a monoid object; it is not assumed commutative. More explicitly, the map $A(S)[G(S)]\times M(S)\to M(S)$ sends $(\sum a_g[g],m)$ to $\sum a_g(gm)$ and is $A(S)$-bilinear. It is natural in $S$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] it uniquely extends to $B\times M\to M$ as a bilinear sheaf map, hence to $B\otimes_A M\to M$. This construction, rather than global lifting of arbitrary sections to generators, supplies the claimed action and its uniqueness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the internal homogeneous bar input.

proof.text: The tensor of $\mathcal M$ is additive and closed by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For fixed $B$, its tensor functor preserves finite colimits: if $L=\operatorname{colim}_i M_i$, the adjunction identifies maps $B\otimes_A L\to N$ with maps $L\to\mathcal Hom_A(B,N)$, hence with compatible maps $M_i\to\mathcal Hom_A(B,N)$, hence with compatible maps $B\otimes_A M_i\to N$. This proves the colimit universal property. In particular [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes the category of $B$-module objects abelian. Then [lem-sfb-modobj-kernels] and [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels] apply to $B$ in $\mathcal M$: equivariant kernels and cokernels are computed in underlying modules, with their uniquely induced actions. Images, being kernels of cokernels, are computed there as well. If the underlying image and kernel coincide, their action structures agree by uniqueness on the same subobject; the resulting identification is equivariant. Similarly a zero underlying cokernel is a zero equivariant cokernel. Consequently the exactness and augmentation surjectivity proved in step 6 hold in equivariant modules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the internal homogeneous bar input.

proof.text: Let $T$ be any internal $A$-module with trivial action. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], $-\otimes_A T$ is an additive functor and $A\otimes_A T\cong T$. Apply this functor to the identities of steps 4 and 5. The maps $h_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$ and $h_{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$ satisfy the same contracting identities for the augmented tensored complex, with augmentation to $T$. The kernel-factorization argument of step 6 now proves exactness in underlying modules, including the split surjectivity onto $T$. The tensor actions $g(p\otimes t)=(gp)\otimes t$ make the differentials and augmentation equivariant. Step 8 proves exactness in equivariant modules. This argument uses additivity and the explicit contraction, so it imposes no flatness condition on $T$.

proof.text:
Define $c_n:G^{n+1}\to G\times G^n$ by
$$c_n(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=(g_0,g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n).$$
Its inverse sends $(a,b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ to $(a,ab_1,ab_1b_2,\ldots,ab_1\cdots b_n)$. The composites are identities by cancellation of adjacent inverse factors. Both maps are continuous because multiplication and inverse in $G$ are continuous and only finitely many coordinates occur. For $u\in G$, $(ug_{i-1})^{-1}(ug_i)=g_{i-1}^{-1}g_i$, while the first coordinate becomes $ug_0$; thus $c_n$ is equivariant for left translation on the first factor and trivial action on the other factors. Linearizing $c_n$ and its inverse, then applying the product/free-tensor identification of step 2, gives
$$P_n\cong A[\underline G]\otimes_A A[\underline G^n]$$
with precisely the stated action. At $n=0$, $G^0=1$ and this is the unit isomorphism $A[\underline G]\cong A[\underline G]\otimes_A A$. No projectivity assertion enters the construction.
